context.guidance: Give each Data Principal a summary of the Personal Data Elements held about them and of the processing done on that data, as §11(1)(a) requires. Where a sharing flow exists, list the Data Fiduciaries and Data Processors the data was shared with and what was shared, under §11(1)(b). Serve the summary through an in-app or request route that Rule 14 describes.

value.fix: Scope every query in dataExport to the authenticated user and stop trusting req.body.UserId. Right now any logged-in user can send a different UserId and get another person's memories, which breaks §11. Change it to MemoryModel.findAll({ where: { UserId: loggedInUser.data.id } }). Look up orders and reviews by the same server-side id or email too, never by values from the client. Return 401 if there is no valid «SECRET» Then expand the export into a §11(1)(a) summary. For each Personal Data Element held (username, email, profile image, addresses, payment cards, orders, reviews, memories, login IPs), list the category, its source, the purpose of processing, the processing done on it, the legal basis and how long it is kept. If any sharing flow exists (payment processor, delivery partner, analytics, etc.), add a §11(1)(b) section that names each Data Fiduciary or Data Processor, says which elements were shared, why and when, or states plainly that nothing was shared. Serve this from a dedicated authenticated route, for example GET /rest/user/data-export, linked from the account privacy page as Rule 14 describes. Log each request so you can show it was answered, and add a test that confirms user A cannot get user B's data by changing UserId.
